Surah At-Takathur (The Rivalry in World Increase) is Meccan.

[Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "The surah (Alhakumu at-takathur) was revealed in Mecca." See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/609.]

﴿Preoccupation with worldly increase has diverted you﴾ — the boasting, the vying in boasting, and the competition in abundance of wealth and number diverted you from obeying your Lord and from what would save you from His wrath.

﴿Until you visited the graves﴾ — until you [died] [addition from manuscript "b".] and were buried in the graves.

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning the Jews. They said: "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and the sons of so-and-so are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so," and this preoccupied them until they died in misguidance [Al-Wahidi narrated it in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 537. See al-Tabari: 30/283, Ibn Kathir: 4/546, al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/610.].

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning two clans of Quraysh: Banu Abd Manaf ibn Qusayy and Banu Sahm ibn Amr. There was boasting between them, so the chiefs and nobles counted against one another, asking which of them was more numerous. Banu Abd Manaf said: "We are more in chieftains, mightier in might, greater in company, and more in number." Banu Sahm said the same. Banu Abd Manaf outnumbered them, so they said: "Let us count our dead," until they visited the graves and counted them. They said: "This is the grave of so-and-so, and this is the grave of so-and-so." Then Banu Sahm outnumbered them by three clans, because in the Jahiliyyah they had been more numerous. So Allah revealed this verse [Al-Wahidi narrated it in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 537. See Ibn Kathir: 4/544.].

Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi informed us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Hiri informed us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us, Abd al-Rahim ibn Munib narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn Abdullah al-Shakhkhir, from his father, who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was reciting this verse: 'Preoccupation with worldly increase has diverted you,' and he said: 'The son of Adam says: My wealth, my wealth. Do you have any of your wealth except what you have eaten and consumed, or worn and worn out, or given in charity and sent ahead?'" [Muslim narrated it in al-Zuhd, no. 2958: 4/2273, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/258.]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm narrated to us, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things follow the deceased: two return and one remains with him. His family, his wealth and his deeds follow him; his family and his wealth return, and his deeds remain." [Al-Bukhari narrated it in al-Riqaq, chapter on the agonies of death: 11/362, Muslim at the beginning of al-Zuhd, no. 2960: 4/2273, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/259.]

Then Allah answered them, saying:

Then Allah answered them, saying:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 102, verses 3–6:

﴿Nay﴾, the matter is not [what you think] with the competing for abundance. ﴿You will soon know﴾ is a warning to them. Then he repeated it for emphasis, saying: ﴿Nay, you will soon know﴾. Al-Hasan and Muqatil said: this is a warning after a warning. The meaning is: you will soon know the consequence of your competing for abundance and your boasting when death comes upon you.

Al-Dahhak said: "Nay, you will soon know," meaning the disbelievers, and "Then nay, you will soon know," meaning the believers. He would read the first with the ya' (yasa'lamun, third person) and the second with the ta' (second person).

﴿Nay, if you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾, meaning: knowledge that is certain. He attached the knowledge (ilm) to the certainty (yaqin), as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is the truth of certainty﴾. The answer to "law" (if) is omitted, meaning: if you knew with certain knowledge, what you know would occupy you from competing for abundance and boasting.

Qatadah said: "We used to say that the knowledge of certainty is that one knows that Allah will resurrect him after death" [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/611 to al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]].

﴿You will certainly see the Hellfire﴾. Ibn 'Amir and al-Kisa'i read "lutaraw(unna)" with a dammah on the ta' (from "araytuhu al-shay'", I showed him the thing), while the others read it with a fathah on the ta' (taraw(unna)), meaning: you will see it with your eyes from afar.

They did not thank the Lord of the bounty when they worshipped other than Him. Then they will be punished for abandoning gratitude. This is the view of al-Hasan.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said regarding ﴿you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounty﴾: "It is security and health."[[Narrated with a marfu' chain by ʿAbdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad in his Zawa'id al-Zuhd, pp. (157 and 390), and by Abu Nu'aym in Akhbar Isfahan, 2/157, in which there is Muhammad ibn Sulayman, truthful but erring, and Ibn Abi Layla, truthful but of poor memory. See also Hannad's al-Zuhd with the editor's commentary.]]

Qatadah said: Indeed Allah will question every possessor of a bounty about what He bestowed upon him.[[It is also related from him that he said: security and health. See al-Bayhaqi's Shu'ab al-Iman: 8/495.]]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Haytham al-Turabi informed us: ʿAbdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamawayh al-Sarakhsi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Khuzaym al-Shashi narrated to us: ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Shababah narrated to us, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-ʿAla', from al-Dahhak ibn ʿUrzum al-Ash'ari, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first thing a servant will be questioned about on the Day of Resurrection concerning bounties is that it will be said to him: Did We not make your body healthy and give you to drink of cool water?"[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah al-Takathur: 9/290, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith." (31); by al-Tabari, 3/288; by al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad, 7/224; and by the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah, 4/311. al-Suyuti added its attribution in al-Durr al-Manthur, 8/613, to ʿAbd ibn Humayd. al-Albani authenticated it in Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah, no. (539): 2/66–67.]]

Abu Muhammad ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-Jawzajani informed us: Abu al-Qasim ʿAli ibn Ahmad al-Khuza'i informed us: Abu Sa'id al-Haytham ibn Kulayb al-Shashi informed us: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us: Shaybān Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrated to us, from Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out at an hour when he did not usually go out, and no one met him at that hour. Abu Bakr came to him and said: "What brought you, O Abu Bakr?" He said: "I went out to meet the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to look at his face and to greet him." Then ʿUmar came not long after, and he said: "What brought you, O ʿUmar?" He said: "Hunger, O Messenger of Allah." The Prophet [ﷺ] said: [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "A".]] "And I too have felt some of that." So they set off to the house of Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayhan al-Ansari, who was a man with many palm trees and sheep, and who had no servants. They did not find him, so they said to his wife: "Where is your husband?" She said: "He has gone to fetch us sweet water." Then, not long after, Abu al-Haytham came with a water-skin, swollen with water, and he set it down. Then he came and embraced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ransoming him with his father and mother. Then he took them to his orchard and spread a carpet for them. Then he went to a palm tree and brought a bunch of dates and set it down. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not pick for us from its ripe and unripe dates?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I wanted you to choose [or he said: to select][[Addition from "A".]] from its ripe and unripe dates." So they ate and drank of that water. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, this is of the bounty about which you will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection: cool shade, good ripe dates, and cold water." Then Abu al-Haytham set off to prepare food for them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not slaughter a milking animal." So he slaughtered for them a young goat or a kid and brought it to them, and they ate. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you have a servant?" He said: "No." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When captives come to us, then come to us." Then two heads were brought to the Prophet (ﷺ), with no third with them. Abu al-Haytham came to him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Choose from them." He said: "O Prophet of Allah, choose for me." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The one consulted is trusted. Take this one, for I have seen him praying, and deal well with him." So Abu al-Haytham took him to his wife and informed her of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). His wife said: "You will not fulfil what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said except by freeing him." He said: "Then he is free." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, has never sent a prophet or a caliph except that he has two intimate advisers: an intimate who commands him to good and forbids him from evil, and an intimate who spares no effort in corrupting him. Whoever is protected from the evil intimate has been protected."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter on what has come concerning the livelihood of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): 7/34–39, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith." It was authenticated by al-Hakim, 4/131, and by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman: 8/483, 484, and by al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar: 1/195. al-Albani authenticated it in Sahih al-Jami', no. (6948). Muslim also narrated it in substance by another route, in al-Ashribah, chapter on the permissibility of bringing another person to the house of one whose consent is known, no. (2038): 3/1610.]]

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: The bounty is soundness of bodies, of hearing and of sight. Allah will question the servants: "For what did you use them?" And He knows that better than they do. This is His saying: ﴿Indeed the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned about﴾ [al-Isra': 36].[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/289, and by al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab: 8/493, and its chain is hasan, but it has a break in continuity. al-Suyuti added in al-Durr: 8/612 its attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh. See the commentary on Shu'ab al-Iman.]]

Then he took them to his orchard and spread a carpet for them. Then he went to a palm tree and brought a bunch of dates and set it down. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not pick for us from its ripe and unripe dates?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I wanted you to choose [or he said: to select][[Addition from "A".]] from its ripe and unripe dates." So they ate and drank of that water. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, this is of the bounty about which you will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection: cool shade, good ripe dates, and cold water." Then Abu al-Haytham set off to prepare food for them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not slaughter a milking animal." So he slaughtered for them a young goat or a kid and brought it to them, and they ate. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you have a servant?" He said: "No." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When captives come to us, then come to us." Then two heads were brought to the Prophet (ﷺ), with no third with them. Abu al-Haytham came to him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Choose from them." He said: "O Prophet of Allah, choose for me." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The one consulted is trusted. Take this one, for I have seen him praying, and deal well with him." So Abu al-Haytham took him to his wife and informed her of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). His wife said: "You will not fulfil what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said except by freeing him." He said: "Then he is free." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, has never sent a prophet or a caliph except that he has two intimate advisers: an intimate who commands him to good and forbids him from evil, and an intimate who spares no effort in corrupting him. Whoever is protected from the evil intimate has been protected."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter on what has come concerning the livelihood of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): 7/34–39, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith." It was authenticated by al-Hakim, 4/131, and by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman: 8/483, 484, and by al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar: 1/195. al-Albani authenticated it in Sahih al-Jami', no. (6948). Muslim also narrated it in substance by another route, in al-Ashribah, chapter on the permissibility of bringing another person to the house of one whose consent is known, no. (2038): 3/1610.]]

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: The bounty is soundness of bodies, of hearing and of sight. Allah will question the servants: "For what did you use them?" And He knows that better than they do. This is His saying: ﴿Indeed the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned about﴾ [al-Isra': 36].[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/289, and by al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab: 8/493, and its chain is hasan, but it has a break in continuity. al-Suyuti added in al-Durr: 8/612 its attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh. See the commentary on Shu'ab al-Iman.]]

ʿIkrimah said: About health and leisure.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: About health, leisure and wealth.

Imam Abu al-Hasan ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi informed us: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt narrated to us: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-Hashimi narrated to us: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan narrated to us in Makkah: ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mubarak and al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, both saying: ʿAbdullah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two bounties in which many people are deceived: health and free time."[[Narrated by Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, p. (2); by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, chapter on what has come concerning the Riqaq, and that there is no life except the life of the Hereafter: 11/229; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/223.]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: That is, concerning what Allah bestowed upon you through Muhammad (ﷺ).

Abu al-ʿAliyah said: About Islam and the Sunnahs. al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The lightening of the laws and the facilitation of the Qur'an.
